"It would survive only if those identifiers or reconciliation controls were wrong."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "If policy requires effective-date reporting or the sample finds failed activation, escalate that specific issue; otherwise close the anomaly as reconciled posting timing."
"Standardizing the reporting cadence prevents visual distortion across reporting periods without requiring structural pipeline changes."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "All source events are unique and cash reconciles to the ledger with zero variance, showing no evidence of fake revenue." Unique identifiers and cash reconciliation support absence of duplicate cash or duplicate source events, but do not by themselves establish that revenue is not fabricated or that underlying entitlements were valid.

"This inference firmly resolves data-pipeline and fraud hypotheses." The evidence makes those explanations less likely, but does not firmly resolve them without validating the controls, source transactions, and entitlement outcomes.

"Backdating or period-stuffing: rejected ... because effective and posted months agree." This is overstated and appears factually inconsistent with the described mechanism: effective dates spread from 1–28 May while postings occur at month-end, so effective and posted dates may differ even though both are in May.

"Observed facts confirm complete row acceptance, unique source identifiers, and exact dollar reconciliation across all dealer import files in `dealer_import_log.csv`." The evidence table specifically identifies the two relevant May files; it does not clearly establish that every import file in the dataset has the same properties.

"The cluster is 17/210 = 8.1% of 31-May rows ... across May it is 0.44% of rows and 3.51% of amount." These calculations are not independently reproducible from the submission because the denominators and query outputs are not shown, although the cited fields are appropriate.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The strongest alternative partly handled is a legitimate posting-time batch process rather than duplicate revenue, supported by unique source_event_id values and reconciliation. The submission does not fully handle the possibility that the reconciliation controls or identifiers are incomplete, or that valid cash postings still mask failed entitlement activation or a downstream event-time reporting defect. Its incorrect statement that effective and posted months agree also weakens its treatment of period-stuffing and timing alternatives.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Correctly quantify and show the event-time versus posting-time comparison for all 90 West annual rows, including counts by effective month and the 17 month-end postings, then explicitly limit the conclusion to no detected duplicate cash/revenue issue rather than claiming fraud and pipeline hypotheses are firmly resolved.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Under legacy routing, South had 219 `case_create` sessions out of 442 legacy South sessions; under NOVA-S1, only 90 of 2,709 sessions reached `case_create`."
"South NO_SIGNAL tickets fell from 51 in May to 28 in June, but service-event data still records 10 May events affecting 9,409 accounts and 8 June events affecting 7,045 accounts."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The drop in logged South complaints is substantially confounded by changed session-filtering rules and pre-authentication drop-offs that never reach CareDesk."

"My inference is that complaint volume was suppressed by channel filtering: 24.0% of sessions (650/2,709) in `ivr_interactions.jsonl` dropped out at the authentication stage without creating CareDesk tickets."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "I cannot determine whether dropped authentication sessions resulted in callbacks without a read-only 7-day recontact trace."

"For routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info)," genuine deflection is acknowledged, although the submission does not fully establish whether authentication abandonment represented complaints.

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Do not expand NovaIVR nationally on current evidence."
"The single next action is a read-only subscriber callback reconciliation query evaluating 7-day repeat contacts across all 2,709 NOVA-S1 sessions."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Material unknowns and decision-changing evidence" clearly identifies two unresolved operational questions and how each could change the decision.
The five questions to Farah address "the exact numerator and denominator specifications," downstream handling, case-creation rules, repeat contact, and expansion criteria.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "underlying network service events remained steady across May and June" is overstated: the submission itself reports a decline from 10 events affecting 9,409 accounts in May to 8 events affecting 7,045 accounts in June, and does not establish that these events are comparable to complaints.
"pre-authentication drop-offs in `ivr_interactions.jsonl` tripled to 24.0%" lacks the prior-period rate needed to substantiate a tripling claim.

"unresolved technical issues went unrecorded" is too strong: authentication abandonment and absent CareDesk cases demonstrate a capture gap, but do not prove that every such session involved an unresolved technical issue or a complaint.

"case-creation in `tickets.csv` collapsed from 49.5% under legacy to 3.3% under NOVA-S1" appears to rely on IVR interaction denominators rather than ticket rows, so the source citation and wording are imprecise.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handles genuine self-service deflection for routine balance and pack-information queries, but it misses the strongest benign interpretation of authentication abandonment: some sessions may have been non-complaint interactions, successful self-resolution attempts, or sessions handled through unobserved recovery paths. Abandonment is evidence of a measurement and journey risk, not by itself evidence of suppressed complaints.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end validation beyond repeat-contact reconciliation: link authentication failures to subsequent contacts and outcomes, inspect the actual case_create and offline-recovery rules, and sample or listen to affected calls. This would distinguish missing complaint capture from benign abandonment or genuine resolution.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission directly cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, for `impact_mw=0` and `cleared=yes`.
It cites `event`, `severity`, and `duration_min` for the one 7-minute `COMM_LINK_WARN` and three `info` records.
It cites `timestamp_local`, `inverter_id`, and `duration_min` for the dates, unit identities, and 13-minute total.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission tests the principal alarming interpretation against self-clearing, zero impact, short duration, and one occurrence per inverter: “rejected because all four events have self-cleared ... with zero generation loss.”
It appropriately treats the warning label as an observation rather than proof of equipment failure: “Labels alone do not establish failure.”
The reasoning is based primarily on one event export, so independent operational channels are not actually triangulated.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It limits the conclusion to the supplied export: “The four observed events represent isolated, self-resolving occurrences.”
It explicitly identifies uncertainty about representativeness: “Confirm completeness before treating it as representative.”
It specifies decision-changing evidence—additional open, critical, recurring, or nonzero-impact events—rather than requesting broad additional investigation.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation “Hold escalation and make no equipment change” follows from zero impact, cleared status, and short durations.
The proposed “one read-only export query for the same date range without severity/status filters” is cheap, reversible, and discriminating.
The stop condition is explicit: stop if the unfiltered query confirms these are the only four rows; reassess if it finds materially different events.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: “Hold escalation; close after one cheap check” matches the low-severity, self-cleared, zero-impact evidence while preserving a completeness check.
The submission does not invent a plant problem from the seven-minute communications warning and correctly avoids operational intervention absent stronger evidence.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “These observations give zero escalation signal” is slightly absolute; more precisely, they give no escalation signal within the supplied export.
The statement that the export has “no plant-wide denominator or extraction filter” is plausible as a data-scope observation but is not tied to a specific cited field or metadata source.
“Zero repeat pattern” should be explicitly scoped to the four exported rows and date range, rather than implying no recurrence outside the extract.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The records could reflect an incomplete or filtered event extract, or a communications-quality issue that recurs outside the four displayed rows. That alternative is not evidence of inverter damage, but it is the reason the proposed unfiltered export check is appropriate.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the exact export completeness test or query criteria, including the plant-wide time range and all status/severity filters to remove, so the stop/reassess decision is reproducible.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `dispatch_blocks.csv` fields and gives reproducible calculations for both the cross-day 31.6% figure and the same-day base-versus-submitted comparison.

It explicitly distinguishes metrics: “Summed absolute block deviation is 379.0 MWh... versus 282.8 MWh” from “absolute net daily imbalance,” and identifies the relevant source fields and 15-minute calculation.
The claim that the headline arithmetic is correct is supported by the exact daily penalty totals and formula: “(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission notices the critical design flaw: “It is a cross-day comparison,” with 28 May being the highest-penalty day.
It constructs the required same-day counterfactual using `base_schedule_mw` against the same `actual_mw`, obtaining approximately Rs 549,664 versus Rs 453,086 and a modeled 17.6% reduction.

It tests plausible alternatives and limitations, including hindsight/post-submission adjustment, variable baseline conditions, and incomplete net commercial settlement rather than treating the favorable result as proof of causation.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission carefully scopes the result: “This within-day association does not establish general causal efficacy.”
It separates arithmetic confidence from causal confidence: “High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation.”
It identifies decision-changing missing evidence—immutable pre-submission timestamps and complete net settlement—and avoids claiming that either 31.6% or 17.6% is a general causal estimate.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to “place expansion on hold” follows from the causal and commercial uncertainty without claiming the pilot has no value.
The proposed “prospective shadow validation across pre-registered matched high-wind stow days” directly tests generalization and timing while preserving operational constraints.
The action is appropriately reversible: “read-only shadow calculation... changes no submitted schedule, plant control, or source record.”

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion preserves the legitimate arithmetic while rejecting unsupported attribution: “Credit the arithmetic, reject the attribution.”
It retains a smaller positive result rather than overcorrecting to no effect: “the defensible within-day figure is ~17.6%, not 31.6%.”
It accurately reports 31.6% as a descriptive 28-to-29 May difference and 17.6% as a modeled one-day estimate, matching the strongest supported interpretation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that post-hoc adjustments would “invalidate the AI claim” is somewhat broad: it would undermine predictive-skill attribution, although post-hoc schedule changes could still have operational value for another reason.

The statement that failure to replicate would “conclude the pilot” may be stronger than warranted unless the prospective test is sufficiently powered and pre-specified, though the proposed multi-event design substantially addresses this concern.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 31.6% improvement may primarily reflect unusually adverse conditions on 28 May and ordinary day-to-day variability rather than either pilot efficacy or failure. The same-day 17.6% modeled reduction is evidence of possible value, but it remains a single-day association because schedule selection, timing, and forecast quality are not independently verified.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain immutable pre-submission forecast and schedule timestamps and preregister a multi-event matched comparison that calculates both the base-versus-submitted DSM penalty difference and complete net commercial settlement.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability

"Declaration: P1001 declared with 90211000." sourced to `declaration.pdf`, line 1.
"commercial_invoice.pdf confirms P1001, 10 units, CHF 126,900 and `air_waybill.pdf` links SHP-000522 to CH-2025-000522."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Observed mismatch is 90211000 vs 90211090, while both share HS6 902110."
"‘Any differing string proves an error’: rejected because the Swiss reference lists 90211000 and warns Swiss/EU strings need not match."
"‘Helios is customs truth’: rejected because its Read Me calls it commercial data, not ruling status."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The open question is Swiss legal code on 4 November 2025."
"Swiss Matrix supports declared code but requires Tares confirmation."
"The only legal fact still unresolved in evidence" and the explicit conditional outcome, "A contradictory code flips decision to escalate; 90211000 closes review."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Helios ... is commercial data, not ruling authority."
"Schema omits system/version/date/ruling authority."
"Whole-string matching across distinct jurisdictions is structurally invalid."
"Resolving schema deficiencies prevents repetitive false positives across Swiss entries."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares/ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive and add jurisdiction/version/date to the comparator."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Mismatch is a control artifact rather than broker non-compliance" is a reasonable interim conclusion but is stated more categorically than the unresolved Tares/ruling evidence permits.
"No record contradicts 90211000" should be qualified as no cited record contradicts it; absence of a contradiction is not affirmative legal validation.

"CHF 126,900 total closes it" is potentially overstated because the submission does not explain why invoice value presentation is material to the code mismatch or what exact broker calculation would resolve it.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 90211090 could be the legally required Swiss code on 2025-11-04 despite the matrix entry, or the matrix could be stale, misapplied to the product, or not an authoritative ruling source. The submission appropriately retains this possibility and specifies Tares/ruling confirmation as the discriminator.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly distinguish the evidence-supported interim control decision from the final legal classification conclusion, and explain why invoice-value presentation is relevant before treating it as a remaining decision variable.

"The only Irish-origin register entry supplied for P1006 is SUP-02, valid 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-31... the shipment date is 2025-09-18."
"The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference=Yes proves the claim’: rejected because the indicator is a declaration field... while the packet lacks a linked supplier declaration"
"‘US ERP origin proves the claim is false’: rejected because `origin-workshop.md` explicitly says Helios is not a preference-proof system"
"‘The expired SUP-02 entry is sufficient’: rejected by its 2025-07-31 end date versus the 2025-09-18 entry date."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The claim is unsupported by packet evidence, but not disproved."
"My inference is therefore limited to an evidence-control failure."
"absence in `supplier_origin_register.csv` is not an inference of false origin or fraud."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Commercial manufacturing country in ERP does not legally settle preferential origin"
"none identifies the supplier route supporting preference"
"Automated check in `review_note.txt` flagged missing ClearView links."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim pending supplier-specific proof, request the declaration and governing rule from Procurement/Customs, and do not clear it as preferential until verified."
"A supplier-linked declaration and applicable rule is the decision-changing proof."
"do not clear it as preferential until verified"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "SUP-03/05/06 plus valid proof could support preference; SUP-01/US would support non-preferential treatment" is directionally reasonable but depends on the applicable preferential-origin rule and the shipment-specific supplier linkage, neither of which is established in the submission.
"this hold is reversible" is plausible for an administrative hold but is not demonstrated solely by the extract showing 0.0% duty; reversibility depends on the customs and operational workflow.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be valid and supported by a supplier-specific declaration or qualifying evidence held outside the incomplete ClearView/register packet; the US manufacturing-country field does not resolve preferential origin either way.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Tie each possible supplier route to the exact applicable preferential-origin rule and document the targeted procurement search or shipment-to-supplier reconciliation before stating what outcome each supplier would support.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 262 `qcore_release_ts` values are exactly 02:10:00" citing `batch_release.csv` and `source_freshness.csv`; "The SOP defines the routine target... but the extract has no timestamp" citing `qc_release_sop.md` and the CSV header.

"The 42 HOLD rows are open/right-censored" citing `batch_release.csv`. The claims are generally traceable and include counterevidence, but the submission does not demonstrate that 02:10 is definitively a defaulted interface timestamp rather than merely coinciding with a snapshot.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The apparent receipt-to-release mean is 45.5 hours, but the SOP target starts when required evidence is available" separates the measured symptom from the SOP mechanism.

"The 42 rows still in the queue are the slow observations" and the discussion of snapshot defaults test survivorship and timestamp explanations, but the causal conclusion that the timestamps are a synchronization artifact is stronger than the cited evidence establishes.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "lab_complete_ts is only a proxy" and "there is insufficient evidence because the required start timestamp is absent" appropriately bound KPI validity.

The table assigns claim-specific confidence, including "Medium-High" for non-routine signals and noting that missing/index-pending COA "may be source lag". However, "represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact" is stated too definitively, and the non-coherent timing of the extracts is not explicitly bounded.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Do not launch the 'one and a half days' KPI yet" and "Can this extract calculate the SOP's routine evidence-available-to-disposition KPI? No" directly reframe the decision around metric validity.

The proposed read-only spot-check is reversible and protects against dashboard misuse, but the recommendation could better distinguish an interim descriptive metric from a KPI and specify a success criterion for validating timestamp semantics.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission rejects "The 1.5-day headline reflects genuine process speed" using timestamp concentration, rejects "Discard the extract as corrupt" using valid monotonic duration arithmetic, and rejects immediate dashboard release using missing start timestamps and right-censoring.
It identifies plausible competing explanations, but it does not fully test the strongest alternative that the 02:10 values could be legitimate release decisions recorded at a common operational time.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Execute a targeted read-only spot-check of 5–10 batches in live QCore and CertVault" requests a small, relevant sample.

The table also requests true upload timestamps and audits of 02:10 batches. This is high-value evidence, but it should explicitly request the event/decision timestamp definition or an event log and reconcile source snapshot times before relying on live-system comparisons.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact" is plausible but not proven by coincidence with the QCore snapshot time alone.

"185 of 262 release timestamps ... are defaulted to 02:10:00 snapshot boundaries" overstates what the available snapshot metadata demonstrates; it establishes concentration and timing coincidence, not necessarily defaulting.

Calling the adjusted result an "evidence-to-release median" is misleading because the submission also states that the required evidence-availability timestamp is absent; it should be labeled a proxy or restricted timestamp analysis.
The submission does not explicitly establish that QCore, LabTrack, and CertVault extracts are not a coherent point-in-time snapshot, limiting confidence in joins and source-lag interpretations.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration may reflect a legitimate operational release or batch-commit convention rather than a measurement artifact. The extract can still support descriptive receipt-to-release and lab-complete-to-release proxies, while the SOP KPI remains indeterminate until event definitions and timestamps are verified.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Request and inspect a small event-level audit log for sampled batches that contains evidence-availability, disposition-decision, and interface-commit timestamps, alongside extract snapshot times. This would discriminate workflow delay from interface timing and establish whether the 02:10 values are true decisions or export commits before any KPI is launched.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with the 24 July ProcureNet snapshot” — cites specific freshness sources and acknowledges the temporal mismatch.
“Revision-B valve supply is two free units ... against four units of revision-B demand” — traces a material conclusion to stock, requests, and restrictions files.
“The firm saving is $20.5k across 8 requests” — the underlying quantities and quotes are cited, but realized savings are not directly evidenced.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: “A semantic-search hit means transfer it”: rejected” using reservation and zero-stock evidence tests retrieval against operational eligibility.
“An exact join on manufacturer part numbers succeeds for 100% of populated requests” — distinguishes identity matching from constraints such as qualification, revision, and reservations.

“The brief assumes search recall is the constraint ... The other 11 requests require master-data hygiene” — useful hypothesis, but the submission does not actually test semantic-search recall or precision for the blank-MPN requests.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “‘actionable now’ still requires current confirmation” — appropriately downgrades confidence because the global stock snapshot is stale.
“available_qty_global=-1 ... is a verification flag, not proof of zero stock” — correctly avoids treating a derived availability field as definitive.
“Actionable now” is still somewhat overstated given the acknowledged 26 June versus 24 July temporal inconsistency and lack of live confirmation.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: “Do not convert raw search hits into automatic transfers” — directly protects against unsafe operational action.
The three-way classification of actionable, needs check, and not transferable provides a prioritized and operationally useful decision frame.

“Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search” and require live CMMS, engineering, and qualification checks — a small, testable, reversible next step with clear decision implications.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects automatic transfer from semantic hits, family-level interchangeability, interpreting negative availability as no stock, and the necessity of an expensive semantic-search system.
For each, it gives contrary evidence and states what could revive the conclusion, such as “live CMMS check” or “documented engineering approval.”

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records,” “live local CMMS reservation and availability query,” and “Receiving engineer and qualification approval” are specific, decision-relevant requests.
The evidence is well targeted, but the submission does not clearly rank which query has the highest expected decision impact first.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “An exact MPN join resolves all 13 identified requests immediately” overstates what the evidence establishes: several exact-identity candidates still face stock competition, revision, reservation, or current-availability checks.

“The firm saving is $20.5k” and “delivers immediate savings” treat quoted external spend as realized savings without evidence that transfers are current, approved, executed, and actually avoid the quoted cost.

“The other 11 requests require master-data hygiene, not an expensive semantic search engine” is plausible but not demonstrated because semantic-search recall and precision were not tested on those 11 blank-MPN requests.
The “actionable now” classification remains stronger than warranted while relying on a stale global stock extract, even though current confirmation is acknowledged.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact MPN matching may handle the populated requests, but semantic search could still provide material candidate-generation value for the 11 blank-MPN requests. The main constraint may therefore be a combination of master-data quality and retrieval, with semantic search useful if it produces additional high-quality candidates that survive revision, qualification, UOM, reservation, and live-availability checks.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a bounded comparison on the 11 blank-MPN requests: obtain the best available maintenance-record identities, execute semantic retrieval, and measure additional valid candidates that pass engineering, revision, UOM, reservation, and live-stock confirmation. This would directly test the central claim that data cleanup dominates semantic search while preventing candidate value from being reported as realized savings.
